lead: Test build 0.8.20 (CI run 39003702169, branch round-0.8.20), the fixes for the macOS results of 0.8.19: the Control Center works next to the DAW on every system, a duplicated track shows "Virus unavailable" again, and the backup folder that the Access installer created as administrator is given back to you. One block per system, about 30 to 45 minutes each. Mark each item, add a note where something looks different, then copy the results at the bottom into the chat.
rules: Second build (CI run 39006712326): fixes for L5 (REAPER crash), the Control Center's window and closing, and the missing Access look on Windows. Items you already passed stay passed; the new items M5, L6, L7, W5 and B5 check the fixes.
Third build (CI run 39010110029): only for B6 and B7 on Windows; everything else is done.
Disposable DAW project only. No firmware or OS update, no "Burn To Flash", no factory reset, no storing patches.
Order: macOS (the Virus is there), then Linux, then the Windows 11 VM, and Windows 11 on this PC last.
Close the DAW before moving the Virus to another machine.

sections.title: macOS
prep: Second build: Claude unpacked it to ~/Downloads/TI-Revive-0.8.20b-mac; install with sudo installer -pkg ~/Downloads/TI-Revive-0.8.20b-mac/"TI Revive.pkg" -target /. First build: Claude unpacked the package to ~/Downloads/TI-Revive-0.8.20-mac. In Terminal: sudo installer -pkg ~/Downloads/TI-Revive-0.8.20-mac/"TI Revive.pkg" -target /
notes: Your Documents/Access Music folder still belongs to the administrator on purpose: M1 checks that the installer fixes it.

items.title: Backup folder given back, smoke test
steps: In Terminal: ls -l ~/Documents/"Access Music". If it still shows root: run "Set up Access Virus TI files.command" from the package folder and look again.
Start Ableton: the Virus track plays, the editor opens.
items.expect: your user name instead of root (note whether the installer or the setup command fixed it). Sound, editor normal.

items.title: Control Center next to Ableton
steps: Let Ableton play the Virus track in a loop.
Start TI Revive Control Center: device info, then back up one bank (default folder in Documents/Access Music).
Export a library through its file dialog; open Nerd mode, Live view.
items.expect: the Control Center connects (no waiting message), the backup and the export files appear, traffic scrolls, and Ableton keeps playing in time without dropouts.

items.title: Duplicate track
steps: Duplicate the Virus track in Ableton and open the duplicate's editor.
Play the original track.
Delete the original track, play the copy.
items.expect: the duplicate's editor shows the "Virus unavailable" page (the LCD says "Virus in use"), the original plays in time. After deleting the original, the copy takes over within a few seconds and plays.

items.title: Greyed controls stay locked
steps: Set part 1's Input Mode to Off.
Click the greyed Input select in the INPUT box (not the ENV FOLLOWER's Input menu).
Turn on help mode (?) and hover over it.
items.expect: no menu opens, the value stays. Help shows "Inactive now: depends on Input Mode ...".

items.title: Second build: Control Center window
steps: Install the second build (see the note above).
Start TI Revive Control Center.
Look at the whole window, then close it with the window's close button.
items.expect: the Access look fills the window, nothing cut off on the right, no empty margin. It closes normally.

sections.title: Linux
sections.where: REAPER via pw-jack, Virus on this PC
prep: Second build: cd ~/Downloads/TI-Revive-0.8.20b-linux && ./install.sh. First build: close Ableton on the Mac, move the Virus to this PC, then install the package that Claude unpacked to ~/Downloads/TI-Revive-0.8.20-linux with ./install.sh (asks for your password once).

items.title: Smoke test and patch libraries
steps: Start REAPER, open the test project, play a few notes.
Open the patch browser and look at the personal libraries.
items.expect: sound, editor normal. The factory libraries appear (they are in ~/Dokumente/Access Music, which builds before 0.8.19 never looked at).

items.title: E175: cable replug and power-on without a DAW
steps: Close REAPER. Pull the USB cable for 10 s, plug it back in, start REAPER, play.
Close REAPER. Switch the Virus off, wait 15 s, switch it on, start REAPER, play.
If it stays silent in either case: do not power-cycle yet, go to L3.
items.expect: sound in both cases. Either way the broker log records the packet sizes; Claude reads it afterwards.

items.title: Only if L2 was silent: one USB reset as a cure
steps: Close REAPER and wait 40 s (the broker exits and resets the port once).
Start REAPER again and play.
items.expect: unknown, this is the question. Sound back means a reset is enough and no power cycle is needed. Power-cycle the Virus afterwards anyway.

items.title: Control Center next to REAPER
steps: Let REAPER play the Virus track in a loop.
Start TI Revive Control Center: device info, then back up one bank (default folder, ~/Dokumente/Access Music).
Export a library through its file dialog; open Nerd mode, Live view.
items.expect: the Control Center connects (no waiting message), the backup and the export files appear, traffic scrolls, and REAPER keeps playing in time without dropouts.

items.title: Duplicate track and greyed controls
steps: Duplicate the Virus track in REAPER and open the duplicate's editor.
Play the original track.
Delete the original track, play the copy.
Then the greyed Input select as in M4.
items.expect: the duplicate's editor shows the "Virus unavailable" page (the LCD says "Virus in use"), the original plays in time. After deleting the original, the copy takes over within a few seconds and plays. No menu opens, the value stays. Help shows "Inactive now: depends on Input Mode ...".

items.title: Second build: duplicate track again
steps: Install the second build (see the note above).
Repeat L5 with the installed package (you tested a build from Claude's machine before).
items.expect: no crash; the duplicate shows "Virus unavailable" and takes over after the original is deleted.

items.title: Second build: Control Center window and closing
steps: Start tirevive-control-center from a terminal.
Look at the whole window, then close it with the window's close button.
items.expect: the Access look fills the window without an empty margin. No "Speicherzugriffsfehler" in the terminal after closing (the GTK warnings at the start are harmless).

sections.title: Windows 11 VM
prep: Prepare: close REAPER. Claude hands over the Virus with VM=win11 scripts/vm.sh attach (stops the Linux broker first). 0.8.20 is installed in the VM with setup.exe.

items.title: Handover from Linux and smoke test
steps: Open the test project in Ableton, play.
items.expect: sound right away, no error 31 in the broker log, no power cycle needed (E179).

items.title: Control Center next to Ableton, file dialogs
steps: Let Ableton play the Virus track in a loop.
Start TI Revive Control Center. Backup: choose a target folder in the dialog, back up one bank.
Export a library through its file dialog; open Nerd mode, Live view.
items.expect: the dialogs accept a folder or file and the files appear there, traffic scrolls, Ableton keeps playing in time.

items.title: Duplicate track
steps: Duplicate the Virus track in Ableton and open the duplicate's editor.
Play the original track.
Delete the original track, play the copy.
items.expect: the duplicate's editor shows the "Virus unavailable" page (the LCD says "Virus in use"), the original plays in time. After deleting the original, the copy takes over within a few seconds and plays.

items.title: Greyed controls stay locked
steps: Same as M4, in Ableton.
items.expect: no menu opens on the greyed Input select.

items.title: Second build: Control Center look and window
steps: Start TI Revive Control Center (Claude installed the second build in the VM).
Look at the whole window, then close it.
items.expect: the Access look now (the setup fetched it from the Access installer), nothing cut off on the right.

sections.title: Windows 11 on this PC
sections.where: boot into Windows; Claude is not available during it
prep: Prepare: in Windows, download the 0.8.20 setup.exe from github.com/derpsn/access-virus-ti-revive/actions/runs/39006712326 (artifact "TI-Revive-msi", GitHub login) and install it. On one of the NTFS data disks ("Volume") create a folder tirevive-0.8.20 for the results. Take the second build (run 39006712326), not the first.

Third build for B6/B7 (CI run 39010110029): download its setup.exe the same way (artifact "TI-Revive-msi") and install it over the second. It fixes the dropouts at 4096 in the first seconds and logs the sound card's rate and buffer size in diag.log.
notes: Do this block last. Reboot to Linux at the end; Claude then reads the folder read-only.

items.title: Smoke test and sidechain
steps: Ableton: the Virus track plays.
Preferences: 3 Outs / 1 Input. Route an audio track into the plug-in's sidechain input, set part 1 Input Mode to Static, play the audio track.
items.expect: sound, and the sidechain audio is heard through the Virus.

items.title: Timing render
steps: A MIDI clip with 16ths at 120 BPM for 30 s into the Virus, 44.1 kHz, buffer 256.
Export audio as WAV into tirevive-0.8.20 as render-16ths.wav.
items.expect: a clean render. Claude compares it with the VM's gap pattern (E141) afterwards.

items.title: Reconnect without the VM
steps: Ableton open and playing: pull the USB cable for 10 s, plug it back in.
Close Ableton, switch the Virus off and on, start Ableton, play.
items.expect: sound comes back in both cases. Silent means E175 exists on Windows too.

items.title: ASIO latency and logs
steps: Optional: choose the ASIO device "TI Revive Virus Audio" (needs 3 Outs / No Input), buffer 256, note the input and output latency Ableton shows.
Run tirevive-usbinfo.ps1 and copy its output into tirevive-0.8.20.
items.expect: latency values noted; the log contains the broker log with the packet lines.

items.title: Control Center look and window
steps: Start TI Revive Control Center.
items.expect: the Access look, nothing cut off on the right. If it shows the plain page: run "Set up Access Virus TI files" from the Start menu once with the Access .msi in Downloads, then start it again.

items.title: Your sound card at buffer 2048
steps: Ableton Preferences > Audio: your sound card's ASIO driver, buffer 2048. Note the sample rate it shows.
Open the test project, close the plug-in window, let the Virus track play for 1 minute. Note the clock time when you hear crackling.
Open the plug-in window and play another 30 s.
items.expect: no crackling. If there is: the times and whether the plug-in window was open. The plug-in log records rate and buffer; Claude reads it read-only afterwards.

items.title: Buffer 4096 and the first seconds
steps: Same at buffer 4096 (if your card offers it): start playback right after opening the project, then 1 minute.
Optional: the ASIO device "TI Revive Virus Audio" at 2048 for comparison.
items.expect: no crackling, also not in the first seconds (that part is fixed in the third build). Note anything you hear with the time.
